messages:
alice: heads up — after yesterday's runtime merge we're seeing a ~6-10% p95 host CPU uplift for small streaming requests. traces point at host-side tokenization + grpc write path.

ravi: saw that in dashboards too. gpu metrics look normal; host CPU is where the delta is. flamegraph upload shows hot stacks at preparse::tokenize and proxy::writev. :eyes:

mei: can you post a tiny reproducer so i can spin it up on staging?

alice: simple streaming example i used: 
```bash
curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -d '{"input":"short chat..."}' https://ingress.redwood/api/v1/stream
```
requests generate many 64-128B chunks; grpc over http2; writev seems called per-chunk.

jorge: hmm — sounds like the mini-frame coalescing got weaker after the kernel selection swap. new kernel selection prefers a short-seq fast path that skips some coalesce hinting.

ravi: profiling stack samples: 
preparse::split_fragment -> grpc::writev -> syscall::writev -> kernel_select::choose_shortseq
we're seeing increased syscall rate.

alice: also noticed kvcache eviction churn on same shard when many small requests hit; that adds CPU on preparse and eviction bookkeeping.

mei: hypothesis: batching heuristics regressed -> smaller micro-batches -> more small writes + kv thrash. quick experiments: increase minibatch window 4ms -> 8ms on staging and see.

ravi: also implement a tiny coalesce in the ingress proxy: buffer up to 512 bytes OR 5ms before issuing writev. should reduce syscall frequency without hurting latency much.

alice: i'll deploy a canary with proxy tweak + batching window bump. will monitor p95 and decode latency.

jorge: quick kernel change idea to prefer coalescing-aware kernel for short sequences when grpc writev is hot. patch sketch: 
```diff
- if (seq_len < 32) return choose_fast_path();
+ if (seq_len < 32 && !grpc_writev_hot()) return choose_fast_path();
```
this keeps fast-path for normal cases but avoids it when writev syscall rate is high.

mei: staging config I'll use: 
\"ingress.minicoalesce_ms\": 8, 
\"proxy.max_coalesce_bytes\": 512

perf-bot: canary metrics posted: p95 host CPU down ~7% after patch, request rate unchanged, gpu throughput unaffected. (auto-post)

alice: great. follow-ups: (1) add unit/integration test that simulates 60B chunk bursts to ensure coalesce doesn't add >1ms extra latency, (2) instrument kvcache evictions per-shard + attach to tracing so we can correlate evictions -> cpu.

ravi: i'll own (2) and add a small telemetry counter per-eviction with shard tag.

mei: i'll do (1) and add a regression test in preparse test harness. also enabling short-lived mitigation flag: \"writev_batching=true\" in canary for 24h.

alice: i'll run the rollout and monitor. if stable 24h -> ship. tagging this triage and assigning owners. :thumbsup:

jorge: small note — if coalescing reduces the number of small writes, we should re-evaluate batching heuristics thresholds (minibatch ms and token count) in the autobatcher; current defaults tuned pre-kernel-swap may be suboptimal now.

alice: agreed — add a follow-up ticket to sweep autobatcher thresholds across kernels.

mei: logged infra ticket INF-2029, linking canary results.

alice: thanks all — update in ~2h after first canary window.
